reviews.text: I have had blink cameras since they first came out and I have to say this last October 2026 update is maddening and nonsensical. If you have blink cameras, then you know. This is being discussed on Reddit as well. The developers need to rethink what they have done to our beloved app. People with multiple cameras are having to scroll through dozens upon dozens of many clips broken into moments… for what purpose? The clip screens are also huge, which requires even more scrolling because you can only see a small percentage of them on the screen. And why are the clips divided into so many different sections? What is the purpose of that? Who has time to scroll through so many clips in the morning? The app was perfect the way it was. Change it back and I’ll add more stars!

reviews.title: The latest update has broken Clips
reviews.text: I am a Blink early adopter, having used the system for almost 10 years now. Most improvements with the app over the years have been positive, but Blink has never had a great Clip management process. Unfortunately with the latest UI update Blink has made it even worse. Clips that used to sort small and in a row (like what the App Store pictures look like) are now large and unwieldy. I can only see two at a time instead of 8 or 9. This completely wrecks my ability to go through a week’s worth of clips and delete what I don’t need and keep what I do, because I can only see so few. Also there’s no ability to sort by date like oldest to newest so I have to scroll and scroll and scroll and scroll and scroll now to get to the beginning of a run. It’s never been easy to do this, even when I could see 8-9 clips at a time. But now it’s unmanageable. PLEASE REVERSE THIS UI! WHY IN THE WORLD DID YOU DO THIS IN RHE FIRST PLACE?!

reviews.title: New revision is terrible.

And we have all the nonsense AI features showing up before and between our ACTUAL subscription filter options. GET RID OF IT. We don’t want it we didn’t pay for it. We pay for the service we pay for don’t clog our filtering capabilities with ADS and options WE DONT WANT AND DONT PAY FOR. And while you’re at removing those useless UI options BRING BACK THE SMALL PREVIEWS or at least an option to choose between NORMAL and SO BLIND I CANT SEE UNLESS ITS ON AN IPAD. These screens are massive and inconvenient and difficult to easily scroll through when on a phone. Your devs clearly implemented a tablet update on a mobile iOS template. Fix it. Renewal is coming up in a few months if this isn’t resolved I’ll probably go to another provider as my backup service. This UI UX is such garbage I use my other service to see what I actually want because it’s more user friendly than this recent update. No one likes it no one asked for it and none of us want it. Fix it

The addition of ai to let you know when it’s a cat not a person moving is a very welcome addition that works well.

A new version of the app has just killed the usefulness completely. Takes so long to open and load content on the app you may as well not bother. The flow on a doorbell should be- notification, open app, speak to person if not home.
Now it’s notification, open app, wait several minutes, see feed and person has gone. Recording has timed out and you don’t know where they are.

Unless this is resolved I plan to move everything over to my Tapo system which is much faster to load and recordings are longer.

Such a shame.

reviews.title: Blink Software Update
reviews.text:
As a loyal, long-time customer managing a large system of 10 active cameras and paying for a yearly subscription, I am incredibly disappointed and frustrated by this recent app "upgrade." This redesign is a massive step backward for anyone who actually uses these cameras for serious home security.
Shifting the clip history away from a clean, compact, easily skimmable list into a bloated, vertical card layout has turned a simple daily routine into a tedious chore. I no longer have a quick way to skim past false alarms. Instead, I am forced to scroll through dozens of individual clips one by one, which induces severe scroll fatigue.
Worse yet, the new layout has introduced severe performance lag. Buffering and loading times for clips have slowed to a crawl, rendering the system almost useless when I need to quickly see what is happening on my property.
I chose Blink years ago for the hardware capability, but this software update treats long-time, high-traffic users like an afterthought. Please bring back a clean list-view option immediately, or you will be losing a dedicated, paying subscriber.

reviews.title: Was great, now terrible

reviews.title: App Updates always seem to break something (and again)
reviews.text:
October 2026 update- they changed the view for clips and opted everyone in by default making it much harder to see what’s been happening at quick glance. And to make it worse, there’s no option to revert back to the “compact” view. It’s wild to me as a software developer that this would have been seen as a user experience improvement. Hopefully they add an option to change back to the old view soon because this is frustrating.


The latest update broke the ability to quickly review a video by tapping and dragging the playback marker in library videos. I used to be able to tap and drag the little circle in the video player to quickly review what motion happened in a particular video, but now the video freezes and has to be played in its entirety. This means a lot more wasted time to go through tons of false positives these cameras pick up. Hopefully this is resolved in another update because it’s really frustrating.

reviews.title: Save yourself £25 a month and don’t buy
reviews.text:
AVOID BLINK CAMERAS. ABSOLUTE SCAM!

I owned Blink cameras 10 years ago, and they did exactly what they were supposed to do without needing a subscription. I bought them again recently, expecting the same basic functionality, but what a disappointment.

If you want to watch the recordings from your own cameras, you now have to pay around £10 a month or more for a subscription. You’ve already paid for the cameras, you’ve installed them around your home, and they’re recording footage, but you can’t watch those recordings unless you keep paying every month.

What’s the point of having security cameras if you can’t watch the footage they’re recording? It’s ridiculous that you have to pay for the cameras and then pay a monthly subscription just to access your recordings.

I’m getting rid of mine and switching to a company that actually lets me record and watch my own footage without charging me every month.

Save your money. I certainly wouldn’t recommend Blink to anyone who wants to access their recordings without paying a monthly subscription.

reviews.title: Needs refining
reviews.text:
Every morning I wake up to at least 25 noticed that a cat is walking on my lawn. Admittedly my cat is often AI described as a fox, a bear, a raccoon, a deer. But, nontheless, I should be able to click on the notifications and mark it as Do Not Notify Me. My phone is set to give an audible alarm at ‘unusual activity, but if my cat is facing the camera it is often identified as a person. So ‘a person is on your driveway’ is a usual alarm notification. It’s usually my cat. Only unusual activity will give an audible notification. That’s great, but can we cut down on the quantity of motion detection notices by marking it as ‘Ok, no further notices’. 
Come on guys, give the user more options to refine the whole thing.

If I’m not by my phone I still want to be alerted to my security. But instead due to some sort of app glitch, server glitch or whatever they have all notifications cached in such a way that when you receive a new notification it will make your watch buzz non stop with alerts for hours on end giving you every alert that blink recorded in the last 48 hours. I’ve been waiting for an update to finally fix this issue but it appears blink doesn’t care and I’ve just about had it and am considering switching to another company. reviews.title: AI Banner will not go away
reviews.text:
Listen: I know you’re probably, as a company, champing at the bit for the robot overlords to take over. However the banner that’s big, red, and seemingly invincible should go away after some time. I am not interested in utilizing whatever AI tricks that you’re peddling. Nothing will make me interested in any AI features you deem “Important!”. When I say nothing, I mean NOTHING. 

What are the AI features you want me to give my location for (it’s already information you have anyway!)? Is this a local model, or is my personal information being shipped to a data farm somewhere, and why should I just trust you without knowing key pieces of information, blindly?

Blink, I’m going to be real with you for a second. Any responsible consumer should know what they are signing up for, where this data is headed, how it will be destroyed (it should be anyway), and a simple opt-out should be made available. This pattern you’ve thrusted upon us is anti-consumer. 

Also, my cameras hardly ever work when we need them to in the first place. Before you say it, we have excellent connection throughout my house and the outgoing connection (which shouldn’t even be necessary with the card module, by the way!) is also excellent. I gave you another star in this review because they worked tonight. I’ll edit it to a one-star when they don’t—which will be tomorrow, if I were a betting man. That star would be pushing it. 

Get bent with the nagging banner.

reviews.title: Awful cameras and app
reviews.text: I don’t know where to even start. I have 3 cameras total. 1 outside camera on my bottom porch, 1 indoor camera outside on my top porch and 1 indoor camera in my living room. Let’s start with the newest camera. The one in my living room. It’s 2 weeks old. App won’t load the video footage to be able to check the camera. Sometimes it just times out, other times the app completely crashes. Onto the next camera which is the bottom porch outdoor camera. Lasted right outside the return window before it completely stopped detecting activity. It is set to the highest level of sensitivity. Yet I can literally do jumping jacks in front of it and get nothing. Now onto the last camera which is about 3 years old at this point. It’s an old indoor camera yet it sits outside year round and still works better than the other 2. A recent problem is the zones where it detects movement. I have most of the zones blocked off so I don’t get a notification literally every 10 seconds from the shadow of the trees moving. Yet it still detects everything within the zones. At this point I’m about to throw all 3 cameras in the trash, cancel my membership and delete the app. They are more of a headache at this point than they are useful. 3 cameras and 3 separate issues. Wish I knew this before buying them otherwise I would have gone with a more reliable brand. What a shame and waste of money. Thank you so much blink for taking my money and in return giving me faulty awful products.

reviews.title: 3 month review
reviews.text:
I bought the set of five about three months ago and I’m less than happy with these cameras. Especially for the money spent on them. I can’t tell you the amount of times we’ve had people on our property and the cameras that should be catching things, aren’t. I had a guy walk up to my house and was on my porch opening a package and the two cameras that should have caught him didn’t, leaving me with nothing to show the police. I was only able to see what it was because my dog was losing his mind and I went to see why. 
They go offline for no reason at all. If I try to check them using the live feature, half the time it acts like it’s loading but never opens. I’ll get notifications that there’s movement at a camera, open the notification and won’t find a video or picture. Videos that should pop up instantly show up on the app to view hours later. The app freezes all the time so I have to close out of the app and re-open it. For the money these cameras shouldn’t have all of these issues. Eventually we’ll be switching these out for Ring.

reviews.title: Never consistent
reviews.text: This app is absolutely horrible. If you want to frustrate yourself then try and do very simple task on this app. For some reason, my doorbell camera is constantly going off-line. And then when I try to bring it back online, there are no helpful troubleshooting steps. The thing has a mind of its own and just functions whenever it feels like it. All of their devices are cheap junk. They work part of the time. When you go on the app and try to arm or disarm your alarm it can take several minutes and then not even do it because the system is off-line. All while saying, it is actively online. The app does nothing more but frustrate the consumer. You have zero control over these devices. When I go and try to look at my front porch camera it takes several minutes to even give me an error message. What is the point of having cameras, if you can’t access them within minutes. I haven’t had any other camera systems, but I would 100% suggest you never use blink. If you were actually trying to keep your home safe. If you were just trying to give the illusion to potential intruders, then these cameras may actually work.
